open_questions.question: Which Chilean authority and operational route will accept her specific Ukrainian medical degree for recognition/revalidation after the 17 August 2026 change, and can it be initiated from Ukraine?
open_questions.why_it_matters: RNPI and ordinary CONACEM certification both require prior Chilean legal habilitation.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Obtain a written, dated response from the relevant accredited State university or Mineduc/recognition authority identifying the current post-Decreto 174/2024 route for her institution and degree.

open_questions.question: Does her Ukrainian rheumatology curriculum include sufficient documented Internal Medicine training to meet CONACEM’s derived-specialty equivalence and possible Medicina Interna examination requirement?
open_questions.why_it_matters: CONACEM can reject inadequate equivalence and its 2026 Rheumatology calendar indicates that some applicants must first pass Medicina Interna.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Send CONACEM an anonymized curriculum, specialty certificate, rotations, hours, assessment records, and work history for a pre-assessment in writing.

open_questions.question: What is the actual RNPI title/specialty processing time and fee, if any, for an individual foreign-trained doctor after recognition/revalidation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The official procedure publishes online availability and prerequisites but no service-level timeline or explicit filing fee.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Request a dated written answer from Superintendencia de Salud before budgeting or travel.

open_questions.question: Can her son support a family-reunification residence/work route, and does his Chilean immigration status meet the statutory family category?
open_questions.why_it_matters: She currently has neither residence, visa, RUT nor work authorization; this lane does not establish immigration eligibility.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Assess the son’s nationality/residence status and relationship documents against Servicio Nacional de Migraciones’ current family-reunification rules.

open_questions.question: Will the intended ISAPRE plan/network credential a doctor only after CONACEM/RNPI Rheumatology certification, and what will it reimburse before then?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No unified ISAPRE specialist-payment rule was found; it is contractual and plan-specific.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Ask the relevant ISAPRE/provider-network contracting office for written credentialing and reimbursement criteria.

unknowns_declared: No official current page found that provides a direct individual MINSAL route for recognition of a foreign-obtained specialty distinct from certification by a university/authorized entity or CONACEM under D.S. N°8/2013. The published RNPI route requires a Chilean university specialty title or CONACEM/other eligible certifier certificate.
No fixed RNPI or CONACEM dossier processing duration was published in the sources reviewed.
No published current RNPI filing fee was found; do not infer that it is free from the separate public-search page’s statement that access to registry information is free.

CONACEM’s foreign-training documentation page was last explicitly updated 2024-09-01, so its RUT requirement and documentary mechanics should be reconfirmed directly before reliance despite the page remaining live in September 2026.

No uniform ISAPRE rule was found proving that an uncertified specialist will be reimbursed or credentialed as a rheumatologist; FONASA MLE’s rule is clear, ISAPRE arrangements are plan/network-specific.
The 286/around-300 rheumatologist figures are a recent professional-journal estimate drawing on the provider register, not an official real-time national count of active practitioners.
This lane does not determine Chilean immigration/work authorization, Chilean RUT acquisition, tax registration, or whether a proposed honorarios engagement meets labour, immigration, and tax rules.
